claims.explanation: Although KF-38789 is annotated as a P-selectin inhibitor, its transcriptional response most closely resembles tubulin/microtubule inhibitors (mebendazole, paclitaxel), and the selective killing pattern tracks with a mitotic/cytoskeletal vulnerability rather than SELP expression. The strongest genomic correlate is intact or amplified microtubule/centrosome machinery combined with loss of DNA-damage and mitotic checkpoints, especially TP53 and CDKN2A/RB1 pathway loss, which sensitizes cells to mitotic catastrophe. Lines with EGFR-activating mutations or mesenchymal/low-proliferation states appear relatively protected.

features.basis: TP53 mutation is nearly universal in selectively killed lines and absent in several protected lines; loss of p53-mediated mitotic checkpoint/apoptosis enhances microtubule-inhibitor killing
CDKN2A loss is enriched in killed lines and supports unchecked proliferation/mitotic entry, a known vulnerability to tubulin inhibitors
RB1 loss co-occurs with killed lines and dysregulates G1/S and mitotic control, increasing dependence on microtubule dynamics
SMARCA4 mutations appear in multiple selectively killed lung and thyroid lines, consistent with chromatin-remodeling defects altering mitotic gene programs
KRAS-mutant lines are enriched among killed lines, possibly reflecting MAPK-driven proliferation and mitotic vulnerability
PTEN loss appears in several killed lines and may increase PI3K/AKT-dependent mitotic entry and microtubule inhibitor sensitivity
PIK3CA mutations are present in multiple killed lines, suggesting PI3K pathway activation contributes to sensitivity
EGFR-mutant lines (HCC4006, KYSE270) are among the least affected, suggesting EGFR-driven survival signaling reduces microtubule-inhibitor killing
NF2-mutant mesothelioma/ovarian lines are in the least-affected group, possibly reflecting low proliferative or mesenchymal state
SF3B1 mutations appear in several least-affected lines, suggesting altered splicing reduces sensitivity to mitotic stress
BRAF-mutant melanoma lines SH4 and SNUC5 are relatively protected, indicating BRAF-driven survival may counteract microtubule inhibition
Annotated target SELP; if expressed, P-selectin inhibition may engage the intended pathway, but the transcriptional signature suggests SELP is not the main selectivity determinant
